script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 14. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Right now, you're probably fine.  But in your mind, you might be suffering about tomorrow, next week, next year.  Anxiety is experiencing pain that hasn't happened yet—and mostly never will.

Worry is paying a tax on trouble that may never arrive. Studies show most worries don't happen. You're experiencing suffering for nothing—suffering real, trouble imaginary. Useful worry leads to action.  If you can do something, do it.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You can only experience the present.  Anxiety trades real now for imagined later.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Worry Audit - What Are You Pre-Suffering?.

Here's your activity: List your current worries. For each: Is this likely to happen? Can I do something about it? If yes, do it. If no, practice letting it go. How much of your suffering is about imagined futures? This helps you distinguish useful anticipation from harmful anxiety.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about worry about what hasn't happened can be applied to worry audit - what are you pre-suffering?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
